detailed_description: 2D-animated, 1980s Japanese gothic theatrical anime cel animation: razor-thin angular ink lines, hard-edged two-tone cel shadows in deep indigo and blue-black, painted backgrounds. Limited, restrained animation: poses are held and only what the shot names moves, with small drifts of hair, cloth and dust in the light; the camera stays locked off unless the shot writes a move. [Shot 1] A medium frame at seated eye level on <Subject 1>, seen from head to boots in the green velvet armchair at the centre of the frame, his stocky body facing screen left; the white marble fireplace with its black iron grate stands at the left, the dark panelled door at the right, the crimson rug on the floorboards below. His black bowler hat lies on the floor beside the chair. His fingers laced together on his knee, he gives one easy shrug, both shoulders rising toward his ears and dropping back down a single time, and then his shoulders stay still, his round face wearing an affable, practised smile, his head tilted, his bright eyes on screen left. <Subject 1> (S1), an American man in his forties with a bright, resonant voice, says amiably, in a well-worn storyteller's tone, <d>[Japanese] まあ、隠すようなことでもない。手短に話しましょう。カンザスの人なら、アレクサンダー・ハミルトン・ガリデブが誰か、説明はいらんのですがね。</d> then his lips close in the smile. In the last moments his laced fingers begin to part on his knee, both hands lifting a little off it, his chest drawing up. The camera holds a static shot.

overall_soundscape: A quiet first-floor room in Baker Street on a summer morning: soft room tone, faint carriage wheels and hooves on the street below through the window, the slow tick of a mantel clock, the rustle of paper and cloth when someone moves.
